tasks.title: Implement ngv2/poc_runner.py deterministic runner-adapter factories
acceptance_criteria: NEW file ngv2/poc_runner.py exists and imports PoC via `from ngv2.contracts import PoC`.
Module exposes constant RUNNER_RESULT_FIELDS == ('exit_code', 'stdout', 'stderr', 'duration_ms') in exactly that order.

make_mock_runner(exit_code=0, stdout='', stderr='', duration_ms=0) returns a callable runner(poc, target_spec) that ignores its arguments and returns the fixed 4-tuple (exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms).

make_scripted_runner(script) returns a callable runner(poc, target_spec) that returns script[poc.finding_id] when present, and the deterministic default (None, '', '', 0) for an unmapped finding_id without raising.

No symbols beyond RUNNER_RESULT_FIELDS, make_mock_runner, make_scripted_runner are added; no Epic-2 child modules (grounding/report/pipeline) are imported; no eval/exec/__import__, no I/O, network, subprocess, globals, or randomness.
`python -m pytest tests/test_poc_runner.py -q` passes against the committed oracle test.

spec.objective: Create the deterministic runner-adapter contract consumed by the DetonationChamber, providing mock and scripted runner factories for tests. Define the canonical result field order and two factory functions that return injectable callables; the real subprocess/bwrap runner is intentionally out of scope and injected at NGv2 runtime.
functional_requirements: Import the PoC input type with `from ngv2.contracts import PoC` (documented runner input type; only poc.finding_id is read by the scripted runner). Do NOT redefine PoC.
Expose module constant RUNNER_RESULT_FIELDS = ('exit_code', 'stdout', 'stderr', 'duration_ms') — the exact tuple/order DetonationChamber unpacks.

Expose make_mock_runner(exit_code: int = 0, stdout: str = '', stderr: str = '', duration_ms: int = 0) returning a callable runner(poc, target_spec) that ignores both arguments and returns the fixed tuple (exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms).
Expose make_scripted_runner(script: dict) returning a callable runner(poc, target_spec) that looks up poc.finding_id in script and returns the mapped 4-tuple.
For an unmapped finding_id the scripted runner returns the deterministic default (None, '', '', 0) and never raises.
spec.interfaces: from ngv2.contracts import PoC; RUNNER_RESULT_FIELDS = ('exit_code', 'stdout', 'stderr', 'duration_ms'); make_mock_runner(exit_code: int = 0, stdout: str = '', stderr: str = '', duration_ms: int = 0) -> Callable[[poc, target_spec], tuple]; make_scripted_runner(script: dict) -> Callable[[poc, target_spec], tuple]  # runner returns (exit_code, stdout, stderr, duration_ms); unmapped finding_id -> (None, '', '', 0)
edge_cases: Unmapped finding_id: scripted runner returns (None, '', '', 0) without raising KeyError.
Empty script dict: every lookup yields the default tuple.
Mock runner called with arbitrary/None poc and target_spec: arguments are ignored, fixed tuple returned unchanged across repeated calls (deterministic).
make_mock_runner invoked with no args returns a runner producing (0, '', '', 0).
Scripted runner returns the exact tuple object/values stored in script for a mapped finding_id.
non_goals: Do NOT author, create, or modify any test file — tests/test_poc_runner.py is already committed.
Do NOT run a real subprocess, open a socket, touch the network, or execute exploit code; the only 'execution' is calling an injected callable.
Do NOT use eval, exec, or __import__; no I/O, file access, globals, or randomness; stdlib only.
Do NOT redefine PoC or any substrate dataclass; import PoC from ngv2.contracts.
Do NOT add fields, public functions, or symbols beyond RUNNER_RESULT_FIELDS, make_mock_runner, make_scripted_runner; do NOT change their names, signatures, or return shapes.
Do NOT depend on or import any other Epic-2 child module (grounding, report, pipeline); the real subprocess/bwrap runner is not built here.
spec.implementation_notes: Single small stdlib-only module. Define RUNNER_RESULT_FIELDS as a module-level tuple. make_mock_runner closes over the four values and returns a nested runner(poc, target_spec) that ignores both params and returns the fixed tuple. make_scripted_runner closes over script and returns runner(poc, target_spec) implemented as script.get(poc.finding_id, (None, '', '', 0)) so unmapped ids never raise. The `from ngv2.contracts import PoC` import documents the runner input type (used for typing/clarity); only poc.finding_id is accessed. Keep the public surface to exactly the three documented symbols.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: No new test data or test authoring — verification uses the already-committed oracle tests/test_poc_runner.py. PoC instances (finding_id, language, code, entrypoint) come from ngv2.contracts; scripted runner exercises a small dict mapping finding_id -> 4-tuple plus an unmapped id.

token_budget_ratio.note: Tests are already committed (tests/test_poc_runner.py); test_tokens reflect verification/iteration against the committed oracle only — no new test authoring per non-goals.
